To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RIs for the commonly requested electrolytes (Na+, K+ and Cl-) in Ethiopian newborns were different from previously published values and that the RIs were similar in newborns and in infants.

the reference intervals for electrolyte values are different in newborns and infant and that the reference intervals of electrolyte values should be applied for the interpretation of values in newborns or infant separately.
the reference intervals for commonly requested electrolyte values in cord blood (from newborn) and venous (from infants) blood samples were established using direct ISE method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the establishment of reference intervals (RIS) for electrolytes in the Ethiopian pediatric population.
the generation of RIs for electrolytes in Ethiopian pediatric population and thus it will be a useful resource to the clinicians and laboratory professionals in Ethiopia.
generating clinically applicable RIs for electrolytes in Ethiopian infants and newborns that can help in the early detection, close follow up and correction of electrolytic abnormalities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RIs of electrolytes in Ethiopian infants are similar to those of newborns and the RIs of Na+ and Cl- were different from previously published values.
the present study provides the first reference values for the electrolytes in newborn and infant Ethiopian population using a new direct ISE analyzer.
the RIs for the electrolytes are different in newborns and infantile age groups, and the RIs should be applied separately.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RIs for the electrolytes in Ethiopian infants are different from the previous studies.
the values of the commonly requested electrolytes (Na+, K+, Cl-) in Ethiopian newborns (cord blood) and infants (venous blood) are different from the previously reported values.

, the present study has generated RIs for commonly requested electrolyte values that can be used for the early diagnosis and treatment of electrolyte abnormalities in Ethiopian newborns, infants and children.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, it is not necessary to generate separate RIs for newborns and infants as the Haris and Boyds rule suggested, and that the RIs for newborn and infant populations can be determined by combining their samples.
the RIs for electrolytes in Ethiopian pediatric population should be generated from the local population.
the RIs of Na+ and Cl- in Ethiopian newborns are lower and those of K+ are higher than those reported from other parts of the world.
